editorial.headline: Printing-Machine Manufacturing, Open Nationally but Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28291 covers the making of printing and binding machinery, with national PMA openness but a clear Bali block for foreign registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28291 is a manufacturing activity for the machinery behind print production. The record describes it as the making of printing machines, including simple press machines, cylinder presses, and rotary presses. Its scope also reaches the equipment that supports print finishing and binding: book-sewing machines, spiral-binding machines, and page-numbering machines. In plain English, this is not publishing, design, or print-shop operation. It is the industrial making of the machines and equipment used to print, bind, and number printed materials.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens this activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar operators, which means the classification is not reserved in the record for only one size of enterprise. A small producer of binding equipment and a larger manufacturer of press machinery both sit inside the same stated activity, provided the actual work remains within the recorded scope: making printing machinery, printing-equipment machinery, and binding machinery. That breadth matters because the scope is defined by the machine-making activity itself, not by the customer, the printed content, or a separate service model.

Nationally, the foreign-investment signal is clear. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. On the national reading alone, this is a foreign-open manufacturing line with no ownership cap below full foreign ownership in the slim record. There is no basis here to add a minimum capital figure, a special licence, a tax condition, or a timing rule. The national facts are simply that the activity is open and the recorded ceiling is 100%.

Bali changes the practical answer. The Bali status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and the record marks `l4_bali_blocked` as true. The reason given is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, so the activity is blocked by the Bali moratorium of May 13, 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is broader still: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk activities for PMA, island-wide and permanently. The honest reading is therefore direct: a foreigner may see KBLI 28291 as nationally open, but cannot register this activity as a PMA in Bali today under the record supplied.
